title: fix(db): log actual chunking strategy used for code
description: Code files imported through `processFileChunking` always report the user-selected chunking strategy (often `sentence`) even though `ChunkingService` detects extensions and routes to the recursive splitter. As a result the UX and logs suggest the wrong behavior. Update the importer pipeline so that we persist the effective strategy/type (e.g., recursive for code, markdown-aware) and surface it in progress updates, reducing confusion when reviewing imports.
notes: Updated chunking pipeline to capture the effective strategy determined by ChunkingService. ChunkingResult now includes `strategyUsed`, we persist it on file records, include it in progress updates, and expose it through EnhancedImportResult/UI. Added progress UI hint and refreshed tests to cover the new metadata.

title: Make coverage upload non-blocking to unblock E2E tests
description:
## Problem
The E2E test jobs (`e2e` and `desktop-e2e`) wait for the entire `checks` job to complete, including the 10-minute coverage artifact upload step. However, E2E tests don't actually need the coverage artifacts - they're only used by the `merge-reports` job later.

## Current Workflow Flow
```
checks job:
  ├─ Lint, type-check, build ✅ (needed by E2E)
  ├─ Unit tests ✅ (validates code quality)
  ├─ Upload coverage ⏱️ (10 min wait - NOT needed by E2E)
  ├─ Enforce coverage thresholds ✅ (validates quality gate)
  └─ Comment PR

e2e/desktop-e2e jobs: needs: checks (blocked by coverage upload!)
  └─ Wait 10 minutes even though they don't need coverage
```

## Research Findings
- **Parallel Execution Best Practice**: Jobs should run in parallel whenever possible (source: https://www.warpbuild.com/blog/github-actions-speeding-up)
- **Dependency Optimization**: Only block jobs on truly required dependencies
- **Coverage Enforcement**: Already validates thresholds at line 106 (test.yml) - the upload is just for archival/reporting
- **Real-world Impact**: One dev reduced workflow time from 9 min → 4 min by parallelizing E2E tests (source: https://marcusfelling.com/blog/2025/optimizing-github-actions-workflows-for-speed)

## Current Code Structure
```yaml
# Line 92-106
- name: Run unit tests with coverage
  run: pnpm run test:coverage

- name: Upload unit test coverage  # ⏱️ 10 min wait
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  # ...

- name: Enforce package coverage thresholds  # ✅ Actual quality gate
  run: pnpm coverage:enforce
```

## Proposed Solution
Reorder steps so coverage enforcement happens first, then upload in background:

```yaml
- name: Run unit tests with coverage
  run: pnpm run test:coverage
  env:
    NODE_ENV: "test"

- name: Enforce package coverage thresholds  # ✅ Quality gate first
  run: pnpm coverage:enforce

- name: Upload unit test coverage (non-blocking)
  if: always()  # Upload even if later steps fail
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: unit-coverage
    path: |
      **/coverage/coverage-final.json
    retention-days: 1
  continue-on-error: true  # Don't block workflow if upload fails
```

## Benefits
1. **E2E tests start immediately** after coverage thresholds pass (no 10-min wait)
2. **Quality gate unchanged**: `coverage:enforce` still blocks on threshold violations
3. **Upload still happens**: Artifacts available for merge-reports job later
4. **Parallel execution**: Coverage upload runs while E2E tests execute

## Expected Impact
- **E2E Start Time**: Immediate (vs. +10 minutes wait)
- **Total Workflow Time**: Reduced by ~8-10 minutes (upload happens during E2E execution)
- **Risk Level**: Very low - only changes job orchestration, not functionality

## Required Changes
1. **test.yml:92-106**: Reorder steps (enforce before upload)
2. **test.yml:97-103**: Add `if: always()` and `continue-on-error: true` to upload step
3. **No changes needed** to e2e, desktop-e2e, or merge-reports jobs

## Testing
- Verify E2E tests start immediately after coverage enforcement
- Confirm coverage artifacts still available for merge-reports job
- Check PR comments still receive coverage summary

title: Optimize E2E blob report uploads with pre-compression
description:
## Problem
E2E test shards (4 web + 2 desktop = 6 total) each upload blob reports using `actions/upload-artifact@v4`. These uploads happen in parallel but each may be slow due to known v4 performance issues with multiple files.

## Current Code
**Web E2E** (test.yml:299-305):
```yaml
- name: Upload blob report
  if: always()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
    path: apps/web/blob-report
    retention-days: 1
```

**Desktop E2E** (test.yml:364-370):
```yaml
- name: Upload blob report (desktop shard)
  if: always()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: desktop-blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
    path: apps/desktop/blob-report
    retention-days: 1
```

## Research Findings (Same as brainstrike-9)
- **Known v4 Performance Issues**: Individual file uploads can cause 503 errors and exponential backoff
- **Proven Solution**: Pre-compressing reduces upload time by up to 90%
- **Playwright Blob Reports**: Typically contain many small JSON files (traces, screenshots, etc.)

## Proposed Solution
Pre-compress blob reports before upload:

**Web E2E:**
```yaml
- name: Compress blob report
  if: always()
  run: |
    cd apps/web
    tar -czf blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}.tar.gz blob-report/

- name: Upload blob report
  if: always()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
    path: apps/web/blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}.tar.gz
    retention-days: 1
```

**Desktop E2E:** (similar pattern)

**Download & Extract** (test.yml:397-403):
```yaml
- name: Download blob reports
  id: download-reports
  uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    path: all-blob-reports
    pattern: '*blob-report*'
  continue-on-error: true

- name: Extract blob reports
  if: steps.download-reports.outcome == 'success'
  run: |
    cd all-blob-reports
    for archive in */*.tar.gz; do
      if [ -f "$archive" ]; then
        dir=$(dirname "$archive")
        tar -xzf "$archive" -C "$dir"
        rm "$archive"
      fi
    done
```

## Expected Impact
- **Per-Shard Upload Time**: Potentially 2-5 minutes → 30-60 seconds
- **Total Time Saved**: Minimal (uploads happen in parallel, but reduces queue pressure)
- **Risk Level**: Low - tar/untar are standard operations

## Priority Justification
**Priority 2 (Medium)** - Lower than coverage optimization (brainstrike-9) because:
1. These uploads happen in parallel (less total workflow impact)
2. Already non-blocking (`if: always()`)
3. Smaller blob reports = less severe than coverage files issue

## Required Changes
1. **test.yml:299-305**: Add compression step for web blob reports
2. **test.yml:364-370**: Add compression step for desktop blob reports  
3. **test.yml:397-444**: Add extraction step after download, before merge

## Testing
- Verify all 6 shard reports are correctly compressed and extracted
- Ensure Playwright merge-reports can process extracted blob files
- Check final HTML report generation still works

## Dependencies
- Could be implemented independently of brainstrike-9
- OR wait for brainstrike-9 to validate tar approach, then apply same pattern here

title: Fix Node.js version mismatch warning in CI/local development
description:
## Problem
CI and/or local development shows a warning about Node.js version mismatch:
```
WARN  Unsupported engine: wanted: {"node":"22.x"} (current: {"node":"v20.19.5","pnpm":"10.17.0"})
```

This indicates that:
- Project specifies Node 22.x as required (in package.json `engines` field or .nvmrc)
- System is running Node v20.19.5
- pnpm is warning about the mismatch

## Investigation Needed
1. **Check `.nvmrc`**: What Node version is specified?
2. **Check root `package.json`**: What's in the `engines` field?
3. **Check CI workflow**: What Node version does `actions/setup-node@v4` use?
4. **Determine intent**: Should we use Node 20 or Node 22?

## Current Evidence
- `.nvmrc` likely specifies `22` or `22.x`
- GitHub Actions workflow uses `node-version-file: '.nvmrc'` (test.yml:48)
- Someone's local environment or CI runner is using v20.19.5

## Potential Causes
1. **Local development**: Developer hasn't updated to Node 22
2. **CI cache issue**: Cached Node 20 being used despite .nvmrc specifying 22
3. **Mismatched config**: .nvmrc says one thing, package.json says another

## Proposed Investigation Steps
1. Verify `.nvmrc` contents
2. Verify `package.json` engines field in root and workspace packages
3. Check where the warning appears (local dev, CI, or both)
4. Determine if this is causing actual failures or just warnings

## Proposed Solution (TBD after investigation)
Option A: **Standardize on Node 22**
- Ensure `.nvmrc` has `22`
- Ensure `package.json` has `"engines": { "node": "22.x" }`
- Update documentation to specify Node 22 requirement
- Verify all CI workflows use .nvmrc correctly

Option B: **Relax to Node 20**
- Update `.nvmrc` to `20`
- Update `package.json` engines field
- Document why we're on Node 20 (e.g., compatibility requirements)

Option C: **Support both**
- Change engines to `"node": ">=20.0.0 <23.0.0"`
- Document minimum version is 20.x

## Impact
- **Current**: Warning noise, potential confusion for contributors
- **Risk**: Low - just a warning, but could indicate actual version incompatibilities
- **Benefit**: Clean CI logs, clear version requirements for contributors

## Testing
Once fixed, verify:
- ✅ No engine warnings in CI
- ✅ No engine warnings in local development
- ✅ All workflows use consistent Node version
- ✅ Documentation updated with correct Node version requirement
notes:
**Investigation Results:**

Confirmed configuration:
- `.nvmrc`: `22`
- `package.json` engines: `"node": "22.x"`

**Root Cause:**
Project correctly specifies Node 22, but something is running v20.19.5, causing the pnpm warning.

**Likely Sources:**
1. Local development environment not using nvm/mise/volta to respect .nvmrc
2. CI runner with cached Node 20 installation
3. Someone running `pnpm install` without switching Node version first

**Recommended Fix:**
Update brainstrike-12 to add pre-install check or better developer documentation about Node version requirements.

title: feat(db): enforce 768D embedding baseline
description: Update the database layer so file_chunks.embedding no longer enforces VECTOR(768). Introduce a migration that converts the column to the dimensionless vector type, records per-chunk dimensions (e.g., via an embedding_dimensions column or equivalent metadata), and rebuilds vector indexes so mixed dimensions do not break ANN search. Ensure migration covers both Postgres and PGlite targets, including data backfill for existing rows and safe rollback semantics.
design: Rescoped after 2025-10-19 decision to stay on 768D. Rather than migrating schema to variable dimensions, add defensive checks so any vector written to file_chunks must be length 768 and users get actionable errors if a provider returns something else.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repository insert/update paths reject embeddings whose length != 768 with clear error messaging
- Integration tests cover successful 768D writes and failing 384D/1024D attempts
- Worker/browser queue code paths surface validation failures instead of raw pgvector errors
notes: Legacy description to be ignored; issue now tracks adding validation to keep embeddings at 768D.

title: feat(worker): guard against non-768D embeddings
description: Propagate embedding dimension awareness through the embedding pipeline. Enqueue payloads with the target embedding set id and expected vector length, fail fast when a model produces a mismatched size, and persist the dimension alongside embedding data for auditability. Update repositories and job queue helpers so desktop and browser workers consistently write embedding_set_id + dimensions, and refresh dedupe hashes if dimensions change.
design: Rescope: queue and worker should assume 768D as the only supported length. Ensure job payloads annotate the expected dimension, short-circuit work when a provider replies with anything else, and surface clear logs/metrics for operators.
acceptance_criteria:
- Embedding queue payloads carry expectedDimension=768 and workers abort jobs when vectors of a different length arrive
- Browser and desktop queue handlers emit user-facing errors if the selected model cannot return 768D embeddings
- Tests cover happy-path 768D jobs and failing 384D/1024D jobs, asserting no partial writes occur
notes: Aligns with 768D standard documented in docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md.

title: feat(ui): warn when selected embedding model mismatches stored vectors
description: Enhance web/desktop import settings to surface dimension compatibility. When the user selects an embedding model, look up existing embedding_sets for the target scope and warn (or block) if dimensions diverge, offering to create a new set where appropriate. Reflect status in embeddings panel and queue progress events so operators understand why a job was rejected.
design: Update UI flows to reflect that 768D is the supported embedding size. Block or warn on models configured for other dimensions, and help users reconfigure hosted providers (e.g., set OpenAI dimensions=768) before queueing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Import settings surface a hard warning when the selected model cannot emit 768-dimensional embeddings (or is misconfigured)
- Users are guided to fix provider-side dimension options (OpenAI dimensions=768, Gemini output_dimensionality=768, etc.) before queueing
- Desktop renderer mirrors the same checks via IPC and unit tests cover incompatible model selection
notes: UI should link to docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md when explaining the 768D policy.

title: docs(test): document 768D embedding policy
description: Capture the new behavior in docs/vector-dimensions.md, README, and release notes. Add regression tests that cover multi-dimension import/search flows (Vitest + Playwright where relevant) and update model registry fixtures to reflect supported dimensions. Ensure change logs mention the migration impact and operator steps (reindex guidance, verifying pgvector version).
design: Refresh docs to reflect the 768D standard, including setup guidance for hosted providers, and add regression tests that ensure the guardrails fire when a non-768D vector is attempted.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/vector-dimensions.md and related guides explain the 768D policy and how to configure OpenAI/Gemini/Cohere to comply
- New tests (unit or integration) assert that non-768D embeddings trigger our validation paths
- Changelogs highlight the standardized dimension decision for db and embeddings packages
- CI passes with the new docs/tests
notes: Include a reference to docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md in the documentation update.

notes: 2025-10-19 sync: Added agent-client loader fallback so desktop assistant status no longer fails when @brainstrike/agent hasn’t been rebuilt. provider-api-key + secrets IPC now pull env keys via the loader, with Vitest coverage in ipc-secrets. Desktop test suite rerun (pnpm turbo run test --filter @brainstrike/desktop). Pending: narrow assistant UI feedback (see brainstrike-31) and align web secrets handling.

title: fix(db): honor configured chunk size for code imports
description: `ChunkingService.adjustChunkingForFileType` clamps `maxTokens`/`overlap` for code files to 384/48 via `Math.min`, so raising the chunk size slider above those values never changes the output. Remove or make those limits configurable so importer settings and CLI flags produce predictable chunk sizes, while keeping enforceable safety caps for extreme inputs.
notes: Walkthrough: 1) Reworked `apps/desktop/src/db-main.ts` to drop the CommonJS pgvector fallback. We now import `@electric-sql/pglite/vector` directly, log structured diagnostics, and throw immediately when the module/export is missing. TypeScript is satisfied with a lightweight declaration shim (`apps/desktop/src/types/pglite-vector.d.ts`) so we keep the runtime strict. 2) Updated `packages/db/src/services/chunking-service.ts` so explicit slider values respect the hard limit while streaming still clamps to the global safety caps. Defaults continue to use file-type heuristics, giving user-configured chunk sizes predictable behavior without losing safety. Tests: `CI=true pnpm test --filter @brainstrike/desktop -- --reporter=dot`, `CI=true pnpm test --filter @brainstrike/db`, full `pnpm check` (desktop E2Es run locally).

notes: Split follow-up UX work into brainstrike-26 (settings model enablement) and brainstrike-33 (assistant picker consolidation). Both linked as child tasks.

Add validation hooks so UI warnings map to runtime errors.

title: feat(embeddings): add telemetry for dimension validation failures
description:
Add logging metrics on dimension validation failures for monitoring and observability. This will help track how often users encounter dimension mismatches and which providers/models are most commonly misconfigured.

**Context:**

- Frequency of dimension validation failures
- Which models/providers trigger errors most often
- Whether users are successfully reconfiguring after seeing error messages

**Scope:**
- Add structured logging/telemetry in validateEmbeddingDimension() (DB layer)
- Add metrics in validateModelDimensions() (Worker layer)
- Track dimension mismatch events with model/provider context
- Consider integration with existing telemetry infrastructure

**References:**
- PR #401: feat: enforce 768D embedding baseline
- docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md

title: docs(db,embeddings): add JSDoc comments to dimension validation functions
description:
Add comprehensive JSDoc comments to dimension validation functions for better IDE support and developer experience.

**Context:**
Recommended by Claude's PR review on #401. Current validation functions have minimal inline comments but would benefit from rich JSDoc documentation including:

- Return value documentation
- Error conditions and thrown exceptions

- TypeScript JSDoc reference: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/jsdoc-supported-types.html

title: research: multi-dimension embedding support architecture
description:
Research and document potential architecture for supporting multiple embedding dimensions (e.g., 384D, 768D, 1024D) simultaneously if future requirements demand it.

**Context:**
Recommended by Claude's PR review on #401 as a potential future enhancement. Current implementation enforces 768D baseline, which meets all current requirements. However, the architecture could be extended to support multiple dimensions if:
- A critical provider cannot downscale to 768D economically
- Benchmarks show significant quality gains from higher dimensions
- Use cases emerge that benefit from mixed-dimension embeddings

**Research Goals:**
1. **Database Schema:** 
   - Dimensionless VECTOR column approach
   - Per-chunk dimension metadata storage
   - Index management for mixed dimensions
   - Migration path from current 768D schema

2. **Application Layer:**
   - Embedding set management with dimension awareness
   - Model registry extensions for dimension metadata
   - Worker/queue payload enhancements
   - UI selection and validation flows

3. **Search/Similarity:**
   - Cross-dimension search strategies
   - Similarity score normalization
   - Performance implications
   - Quality trade-offs

4. **Migration Strategy:**
   - Breaking changes assessment
   - Backward compatibility requirements
   - Data migration tooling
   - Rollback safety

**Deliverables:**
- Architecture decision document (ADR)
- Proof-of-concept implementation (if feasible)
- Cost/benefit analysis
- Migration complexity assessment
- Recommendation: extend or keep 768D baseline

**Note:** This is exploratory research, not active development. The 768D baseline is working well and meets all current requirements per the embedding dimensions explainer.

**References:**
- PR #401: feat: enforce 768D embedding baseline
- docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md
- Current pgvector schema in migrations
notes: This research was already completed. The decision to standardize on 768D is documented in docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md. Multi-dimension support was evaluated and rejected in favor of the simpler 768D baseline approach, which meets all current requirements without the complexity of schema migrations and mixed-dimension handling.

Add collapsible per-provider model lists that toggle availability, surface search/filter for model names, and sync enabled state to assistant preferences. title: feat(ui): consolidate assistant model picker
description: Replace the per-provider cards with a single model dropdown/list populated from the enabled settings selection. Group models by provider with badges, highlight the active choice, and add inline search. Handle long lists via typeahead or virtualization so the right panel stays compact.
notes:
**FIXED: Model Picker Works Reliably Now**

**Root Cause:**
The model picker failed because the store used TWO separate fields:
- `selectedProvider: "openai"`
- `modelsByProvider: { openai: "gpt-4o" }`

This created race conditions - the UI and store could be out of sync during updates.

**Solution: Simpler Architecture**
Refactored to use a SINGLE source of truth:
- `selectedModel: "openai::gpt-4o"` (composite key)
- Provider is derived when needed: `selectedModel.split("::")[0]`

**Changes:**
1. **Store** (assistant-preferences-store.ts):
   - Replaced `selectedProvider` with `selectedModel` (composite key)
   - Removed `setProvider()`, `setProviderAndModel()`
   - Simplified `setModel(compositeKey)` - just sets one field
   - Added `getSelectedProvider()` to derive provider from composite key
   - Migration code for old localStorage data

2. **Wrapper** (assistant-ui-panel-wrapper.tsx):
   - Removed `pendingProviderRef` complexity
   - Removed provider derivation logic
   - `handleModelChange` now just calls `setModel(compositeKey)`
   - Much simpler, fewer lines of code

3. **UI** (assistant-ui-panel.tsx):
   - Removed `onProviderChange` callback (not needed)
   - `onModelChange` receives composite key only
   - Removed legacy provider header component

4. **Tests**: All updated and passing (42 preferences tests, 185 UI tests)

**Benefits:**
- Eliminates race conditions by design (single field update)
- Matches UI's existing composite key usage ("provider::model")
- 50+ fewer lines of complex state coordination code
- No pending refs, no provider derivation, no atomic update hacks
- Easier to reason about and maintain

**Verification:**
- ✅ All type-checks pass
- ✅ All unit tests pass (42/42 preferences, 185/185 UI)
- ✅ Store migration tested for backward compatibility
- ✅ Composite key format validated throughout

The model picker now works reliably across all providers with clean, simple code.

**Post-Merge Bug Fix (PR #406):**
After merging to main, chatgpt-codex-connector identified a critical bug where composite keys were being compared directly against plain model IDs in the `ProviderModelHeader` component. This caused:
- Selected option never found
- Summary banner stuck on "Select a provider and model"
- Dropdown in perpetual "unselected" state

Fixed by extracting the model name from composite key before comparisons:
- Added `modelName = selectedModel.split('::')[1]` extraction
- Updated all comparisons to use `modelName` instead of `selectedModel`
- PR #406 created, rebased onto main, reviewed and approved
- All UI tests passing (3/3)
- Claude GitHub Actions review: APPROVE ✅
- Ready for merge

title: feat(db): enable true token-based chunk sizing
description: The chunker estimates token counts with a fixed 4 chars/token heuristic, which drifts badly on code and markdown. Wire `tokenTrueSizing` through the importer so we sample real token counts (using `countTokensAccurate` or a fast tokenizer) and size recursive/sentence splitters by measured tokens. Expose controls to toggle the behavior and verify chunks stay within requested token budgets.
notes: Recent chunker refactor removed hard 384/48 code clamps and introduced global safety caps, so user-selected sizes now apply. Remaining gap to close this issue is wiring true token measurement (`tokenTrueSizing` + accurate token counter) so chunk budgets use real token counts rather than the 4 chars/token heuristic.

- `selectedModel: "openai::gpt-4o"` (composite key)
- Provider is derived when needed: `selectedModel.split("::")[0]`

**Changes:**
1. **Store** (assistant-preferences-store.ts):
   - Replaced `selectedProvider` with `selectedModel` (composite key)
   - Removed `setProvider()`, `setProviderAndModel()`
   - Simplified `setModel(compositeKey)` - just sets one field
   - Added `getSelectedProvider()` to derive provider from composite key
   - Migration code for old localStorage data

2. **Wrapper** (assistant-ui-panel-wrapper.tsx):
   - Removed `pendingProviderRef` complexity
   - Removed provider derivation logic
   - `handleModelChange` now just calls `setModel(compositeKey)`
   - Much simpler, fewer lines of code

3. **UI** (assistant-ui-panel.tsx):
   - Removed `onProviderChange` callback (not needed)
   - `onModelChange` receives composite key only
   - Removed legacy provider header component

4. **Tests**: All updated and passing (42 preferences tests, 185 UI tests)

**Benefits:**
- Eliminates race conditions by design (single field update)
- Matches UI's existing composite key usage ("provider::model")
- 50+ fewer lines of complex state coordination code
- No pending refs, no provider derivation, no atomic update hacks
- Easier to reason about and maintain

**Verification:**
- ✅ All type-checks pass
- ✅ All unit tests pass (42/42 preferences, 185/185 UI)
- ✅ Store migration tested for backward compatibility
- ✅ Composite key format validated throughout

The model picker now works reliably across all providers with clean, simple code.

title: feat(db): support embedding models with non-768 dimensions
description: `file_chunks.embedding` is declared as `VECTOR(768)` while the model registry exposes 384- and 1024-dimension models. Selecting them in the importer causes insert failures. Update schema/repositories to store embeddings with the model’s native dimension (e.g., via dynamic `embedding_sets` metadata or flexible vector column), validate dimensions before enqueueing jobs, and surface a clear warning in the UI if a chosen model is incompatible.
design: Decision: standardize on 768-dimensional embeddings across the stack. Hosted providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere) can emit 768D vectors via their dimension controls, so we avoid a disruptive schema migration. Epic now tracks guardrails to enforce the 768D baseline and documentation to communicate the policy.
notes: Standardize on 768D; see docs/20251019-embedding-dimensions-explainer.md for rationale.

title: fix(file-import): remove unsafe casts in streaming chunk pipeline
description:
`processFileChunkingStreamPath` in `packages/file-import/src/chunking.ts` materializes stream results into `batch: FileChunk[] = [] as unknown as FileChunk[]` and repeatedly casts streamed chunks (`ch as unknown as FileChunk`). We should thread the concrete chunk type through `ChunkingService.chunkContentStream` and flush batches without double casting so TypeScript can verify shape changes at compile time.

While touching this path, audit the streaming accumulator for large files. Today we only flush when `batch.length >= streamBatchSize` (default 250). Add a safeguard (e.g., capped `streamBatchSize`, chunk size estimate, or measured byte budget) so arbitrarily large overrides can’t hold thousands of chunks in memory before flushing.

title: add streaming chunk coverage to file-import tests
description: The new `ChunkingService.chunkContentStream` / `processFileChunkingStreamPath` path isn’t exercised in tests. Create unit coverage in `packages/file-import/src/chunking.test.ts` (or an integration sibling) that streams large synthetic input, forces multiple `flushBatch` invocations, and asserts batch clearing, strategy resolution, and repository calls. This guards against regressions in streaming memory usage and ensures batching logic behaves under load.
notes: Patch coverage only hits ~58% for `packages/file-import/src/chunking.ts`; 61 new lines are currently untested. Primary gaps are `processFileChunkingStreamPath` (batch accumulation / flush path), the `flushBatch` helper, and the progress-update branch in the streaming loop. Add tests that stream enough synthetic content to trigger multiple flush cycles, assert batch clearing and repository interactions, and cover the progress callback. This should lift the patch coverage for this file back above the project baseline.

title: add pgvector failure-mode coverage for desktop DB bootstrap
description: `apps/desktop/src/db-main.ts` now throws immediately when `@electric-sql/pglite/vector` fails to load, but we only exercise the happy path in `db-main.*.test.ts`. Add tests that simulate module resolution failures or missing vector exports and assert the thrown error messages/log payloads so future refactors don’t accidentally reintroduce silent fallbacks.
notes: Patch coverage report shows `apps/desktop/src/db-main.ts` at ~67% with 21 new lines missing tests. The uncovered paths are the pgvector failure branch (when the import throws or returns a module without `vector`), and the structured logging payload we emit before rethrowing. Add tests that mock `@electric-sql/pglite/vector` to throw or return `{}` so we assert the error message and logged `attempts` array, bringing the patch coverage above baseline.

title: ui: surface tokenizer runtime status in import settings
description:
### Summary
Add a lightweight visual indicator in the import settings panel (and other token-sizing surfaces) showing whether the wasm-backed tiktoken counter is active or we’re in heuristic fallback mode. This came up during review of the token-based chunk sizing work as a useful UX affordance.

### Why
- Gives users immediate feedback about the tokenizer backend after the lazy tiktoken load completes
- Improves debugging/support when the wasm module fails to load and we silently fall back to the heuristic
- Complements the new token sizing toggle and token cap inputs introduced alongside token-based chunk sizing

### Scope / Implementation Notes
- Token utilities should expose the current backend status (wasm vs fallback) in a lightweight observable/promise so UI can react to transitions
- Add a status pill or icon next to “Accurate token sizing,” with tooltip text such as “Using fast wasm tokenizer” vs “Using heuristic estimate”
- Log transitions so we can verify behavior in tests

### Testing
- Unit tests for the status helper in utils
- Component test for the settings panel indicator defaulting to fallback then switching to wasm when available
- Playwright regression in the database settings flow verifying the indicator updates when we purposely trigger a fallback scenario

title: Optimize coverage artifact upload with pre-compression
description:
## Problem
The `Upload unit test coverage` step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` takes 10+ minutes to complete, blocking the entire workflow. This uses `actions/upload-artifact@v4` with a glob pattern `**/coverage/coverage-final.json` that scans the entire workspace.

## Research Findings
- **Known v4 Performance Issues**: GitHub users report workflows going from 2 min → 1+ hour after migrating to upload-artifact@v4
- **Root Cause**: v4 uploads files individually; when there are many files, this causes exponential backoff retries with 503 server errors
- **Proven Solution**: Pre-compressing files before upload reduces time by up to 90% (source: https://thomasbillington.co.uk/2023/01/08/speed-up-upload-artifact-action.html)
- **Why It Works**: Single tar.gz file = single upload vs. multiple individual file uploads with retry overhead

## Current Code (test.yml:97-103)
```yaml
- name: Upload unit test coverage
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: unit-coverage
    path: |
      **/coverage/coverage-final.json
    retention-days: 1
```

## Proposed Solution
```yaml
- name: Prepare coverage for upload
  run: |
    mkdir -p coverage-bundle
    find . -name "coverage-final.json" -path "*/coverage/*" -exec cp --parents {} coverage-bundle/ \;
    tar -czf coverage-bundle.tar.gz coverage-bundle/

- name: Upload unit test coverage
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: unit-coverage
    path: coverage-bundle.tar.gz
    retention-days: 1
```

## Required Changes
1. **Upload step** (test.yml:92-103): Add tar compression before upload
2. **Download step** (test.yml:446-450): Extract tar after download
3. **Merge coverage step** (test.yml:452-476): Update to handle extracted structure

## Expected Impact
- **Time Reduction**: 10 minutes → ~30-60 seconds (90%+ improvement)
- **No Behavioral Change**: Coverage merging and reporting work identically
- **Risk Level**: Low - tar/untar are standard Unix operations

## Testing
- Verify coverage files are correctly bundled and extracted
- Ensure merge-reports job still finds all coverage-final.json files
- Check Codecov upload still works
notes:
**Updated Research (January 2025):**

## Key Findings from Latest Documentation

### Compression Strategy Decision
**Two valid approaches:**

**Option A: TAR (uncompressed) + let upload-artifact compress**
```yaml
tar -cvf coverage-bundle.tar coverage-bundle/
# upload-artifact@v4 will compress with default level 6
```

**Option B: TAR.GZ (pre-compressed) + disable upload-artifact compression**
```yaml
tar -czf coverage-bundle.tar.gz coverage-bundle/
# Set compression-level: 0 to avoid double compression
```

### upload-artifact@v4 Compression Details
- **Default compression level:** 6 (same as GNU Gzip)
- **Range:** 0-9 (0 = no compression, 9 = maximum)
- **Recommendation for pre-compressed files:** compression-level: 0
- **Performance:** For large/incompressible files, level 0 = significantly faster uploads

### Breaking Changes to Note
- **v3 deprecated:** As of Jan 30, 2025, v3 no longer supported
- **No incremental uploads:** Cannot upload to same artifact name multiple times in v4
- **Chunk timeout:** Default reduced from 5min → 30sec (can cause issues on slow networks)
- **Hidden files:** Excluded by default in v4.4+

### Performance Claims (Official)
- "Uploads are significantly faster, upwards of 90% improvement in worst case scenarios"
- Compression trade-off: Higher = smaller artifacts but slower uploads

### Recommended Approach for brainstrike-9
Use **Option A (uncompressed TAR)** because:
1. Simpler (fewer compression steps)
2. Lets upload-artifact's optimized compression handle it
3. Coverage JSON files compress well (text-based)
4. Default level 6 balances speed vs size
5. Can tune `compression-level` later if needed

### Implementation Example
```yaml
- name: Bundle coverage files
  run: |
    mkdir -p coverage-bundle
    find . -name "coverage-final.json" -path "*/coverage/*" -exec cp --parents {} coverage-bundle/ \;
    tar -cvf coverage-bundle.tar coverage-bundle/

- name: Upload unit test coverage
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: unit-coverage
    path: coverage-bundle.tar
    retention-days: 1
    # compression-level: 6 is default (can reduce to 0-2 for speed if artifact size OK)
```

### Download/Extract
```yaml
- name: Download coverage
  uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: unit-coverage
    path: .

- name: Extract coverage
  run: tar -xvf coverage-bundle.tar
```
